page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge is an entry-level virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.e server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 4 physical cores. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any bundled local storage, dedicated GPUs, or baseline network bandwidth, and relies on the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1199.89 and 3141.11 respectively, categorizing its raw compute performance as weak (bottom 25%). Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 716.0 and 657.0 fall into the poor category (bottom 10%). Cryptographic and decompression tasks also show limited throughput, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 688.63 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 7.01 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge is its shared CPU allocation and lack of dedicated baseline network bandwidth, which limits its utility for sustained high-throughput applications. However, this resource profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for budget-conscious scenarios where dedicated hardware is unnecessary. It is best suited for low-demand workloads such as basic static web serving, software development testing, lightweight Redis operations, and non-critical background tasks.
